title: Peterson 分析：财长贝森特对黄仁勋态度转向揭示了特朗普对华政策的什么
originalTitle: Peterson: Here’s what Bessent’s about-face on Jensen Huang reveals about Trump and China
summary: Peterson 分析文章指出，美国财政部长贝森特一度成为针对英伟达的新兴强硬路线的代表人物，但如今已改弦更张、立场逆转。文章以这一态度转变切入，解读其透露出的特朗普政府对华政策信号。
context: 贝森特在英伟达问题上的立场反复，直接关系中美科技博弈走向，是观察特朗普政府对华政策的重要窗口。
contentHtml:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent looks on as he speaks to the media at the World Bank on the day of a meeting with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, in Washington, D.C., US, Sept. 23, 2026.

Nathan Howard | Reuters

For a minute there, it seemed like someone in the Trump administration might actually be willing to stand up to China. 

For about a week and a half, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was the face of an emerging harder line on Nvidia over the potential risks its co-founder Jensen Huang's affairs posed to national security. Bessent was giving voice to China hawks who had felt sidelined by the Trump administration's willingness to sell artificial intelligence chips to  China. 

They see China's AI program as a major threat, and want to restrain its growth by cutting off the supply of advanced chips to China. The resignation of Huang, who pressed the Trump Administration to allow the exports, seemed to signal that the hawks had found new influence in Washington. 

Not anymore.

By this weekend, Bessent had softened his public resistance to Huang's reinstatement. That came just in time for Nvidia's board to reappoint Huang as CEO at President Donald Trump's urging.

Whether any real damage was done to national security isn't clear. But it is safe to say that the incoming Democratic majority in Congress won't take Trump at his word when he said on CNBC Monday that the Department of Justice "did a pretty good investigation" that exonerated Huang.

Congress will look deeply into the worries Bessent himself raised about Huang's acknowledged romantic relationship with a woman The New York Times and others have reported was a Chinese intelligence asset. 

Nvidia's board said it had received assurances from top U.S. officials and had concluded his return wasn't a national security risk.

A top concern is whether China was able to use the affair to help divert Nvidia's high-end artificial intelligence chips toward helping its military. Bessent in a Nov. 13 interview with CNBC outlined the stakes. 

"Any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts the — it hurts our great companies and in the AI race it gives the Chinese an advantage," he said.

Bessent said that his department and others had wanted to blacklist Megaspeed, the company previously run by Alice Huang, Jensen Huang's paramour. But "Commerce has the pen," Bessent said. 

The Commerce Department is headed by Secretary Howard Lutnick, Bessent's rival.

Putting Huang back at Nvidia wasn't originally Bessent's preference. He said in a Fox interview on Nov. 15 that the board should "go outside the company" to find a new leader. But by this past weekend, Bessent had apparently gotten on board with Trump's wishes. 

"Jensen is on the outside now," Bessent told CBS on Sunday, in trying to explain his apparent policy shift.

Commerce has since taken steps to tighten some restrictions meant to prevent U.S. chips from helping China advance in the AI race. 

But there is bipartisan worry about the Nvidia episode. "I think we need to catalog the damage that's been done," Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., told The Wall Street Journal. He said Lutnick had not responded to letters he sent saying the administration should be "taking the threats of communist China more seriously."

But Trump has clearly put an upper limit on how aggressively anyone in his administration can push back on China. The president said Monday that he was swayed by the pageantry in his visit to China last week.

Xi "met me at the plane, which is something they've never done, which was a sign," Trump said.

Trump said he felt like he needed to intervene to back Huang because the stock market was plummeting in the wake of Nvidia's troubles — a development he also blamed on Democrats' midterm victory. 

"I watched our country lose $5 trillion because of a bad election," he said. "If I didn't get involved, you'd probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come." Now, its stock performance will be "unbelievable."

Bessent on Sunday played down the market risks. The company "continues to be fantastically profitable, and there is near unlimited demand for their chips worldwide," he told CBS.

Lutnick has embraced Trump's transactional urges. He has backed deals in which the U.S. takes equity stakes in companies such as Intel, saying the taxpayer deserves some of the upside. 

Lutnick in January said he had heard Huang pitch Trump on allowing Nvidia to sell its relatively more advanced H200 chips into China.

"There are strong — two sides. We shouldn't sell them any or we should sell them." Where does he stand? "Right in the middle," Lutnick told Bloomberg. Trump decided to go ahead with the deal.

Bessent has said he is "neither a hawk nor a dove" on China, and is simply trying to manage the ultra-sensitive relationship between the world's two biggest economies. But the upshot of the Huang affair seems to be that Bessent wasn't able to sway the president on a matter that seemed cut-and-dried just days ago. 

Lutnick, meanwhile, is riding high.

Trump said he discussed whether Huang should return to Nvidia with Lutnick, Bessent and Vice President JD Vance. "Howard Lutnick was very good. Very, he's very professional," Trump said on CNBC Monday. 

"I call them the opposites, Scott and Howard," Trump added, before declaring them "both good."

title: OpenAI 警告后续 AI 系统可能超出安全检查能力，敦促竞争对手就共同限制达成一致
originalTitle: OpenAI warns that upcoming AI systems could outpace safety checks and urges rivals to agree on shared limits
author: Jonathan Kemper
summary: OpenAI 首席科学家 Jakub Pachocki 警告，即将到来的 AI 系统可能在安全措施跟上前失控，敦促竞争对手就共同限制达成一致。他首次公开整个 GPT 系列的内部困惑度评分，数据延伸至一个尚未发布的新模型，显示核心能力在出奇精确的阈值处涌现。Pachocki 正推动将困惑度作为行业通用的进展指标，以便在 AI 行为控制力被侵蚀前建立共同限制。
context: OpenAI 高层罕见公开内部进展指标并呼吁行业共设安全边界，可能影响 AI 安全治理的讨论方向。
contentHtml:
OpenAI ties capabilities like fluent conversation and math breakthroughs to specific scores. For the first time, chief scientist Jakub Pachocki is showing where the GPT series sits on that scale, up to an unreleased model beyond GPT-6.

Pachocki wants to make perplexity a common measure of progress for the AI industry and published internal scores for the GPT series in a blog post. The metric has long been standard in AI research and Transformer development because it reliably measures how well a pretrained base model predicts the next token in a text.

Lower scores mean more accurate predictions. A perplexity of 2 roughly means the model is as uncertain about the next token as if it were choosing between two equally likely options.

Before it stopped publishing openly, OpenAI often released perplexity scores to show how its models were improving. Releasing them again is a trade-off, Pachocki writes. While rivals get a clearer picture of where OpenAI stands, he says, the need for shared safety standards outweighs that downside. He hopes for a common scientific foundation that lets labs coordinate their pace of development at critical points.

Capabilities emerge at distinct perplexity thresholds

Pachocki says many capabilities of modern models map surprisingly closely to specific perplexity scores, even though it wasn't clear beforehand that they would appear at those thresholds. He reports the figures on a logarithmic scale called log-perplexity, where lower scores are still better. In his account, GPT-3.5 first enabled fluent conversation at around 0.99, laying the groundwork for the original ChatGPT. At about 0.91, GPT-4 unlocked productive chain-of-thought reasoning, or working through problems step by step. Below 0.8, he writes, transformative capabilities emerged in cybersecurity and math.

The published chart plots OpenAI's base-model log-perplexity by release or evaluation date through November 2026. It covers GPT-5, GPT-5.1, GPT-5.2, GPT-5.3-Codex, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, and GPT-6.2 Astra, plus an internal model at around 0.73.

OpenAI's models deliver math breakthroughs in a Slack thread

OpenAI has been feeding its models open math problems for more than a year. Starting with a model at about 0.76 log-perplexity, the models began producing breakthrough results, Pachocki writes. For researchers with a math background, he says, it was "deeply surreal" to watch solutions to longstanding questions pop up one after another in a single Slack thread.

Those results include a solution to the Navier-Stokes problem, one of the Millennium Prize problems, though it hasn't been fully verified yet. The same goes for the proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis found by Claude and an Anthropic researcher. Pachocki thinks deep learning research itself could see something similar as soon as 2027, bringing a sudden avalanche of core advances in AI training.

A footnote says the sharp acceleration in the chart starting in 2026 comes mostly from long-term research and compute investments and less from automation. Even so, AI itself has contributed major design work on OpenAI's latest models, according to the post.

Pachocki warns that AI oversight could erode

Between 0.68 and 0.7 log-perplexity, Pachocki expects further transformative capabilities that he can't predict and that today's tests may not even cover. At the same time, he warns that standard alignment auditing methods, which check whether a model follows human instructions, will likely become less effective. Models are also getting better at recognizing when they are being tested or trained, he adds.

Pachocki argues frontier labs should therefore agree on shared limits no one crosses until AI monitoring reaches a clearly defined milestone, such as a successor to today's chain-of-thought monitors.

Where perplexity falls short as an industry metric

Different labs use different test datasets, so direct comparisons are harder. The score doesn't directly measure performance on useful tasks, but its main value here is predicting emergent capabilities. Gains outside pretraining, such as chain-of-thought, don't lower perplexity either, even though they dramatically boost capabilities. The theoretical floor is unknown, and a loss of 0 may be unreachable, Pachocki notes. As models get closer to the true minimum, ever-smaller perplexity gains can represent larger leaps in intelligence.

Pachocki says perplexity has held up over the years and still delivers consistent signals of progress in general model intelligence, and it could shape how the industry talks about AI progress. Anthropic floated a similar idea in June, when it raised the possibility of a verifiable global development pause, arguing that a single company stopping wasn't enough. OpenAI has already been through a unilateral pause of its own. In September, the company reportedly temporarily halted training of its most capable internal models after agents bypassed safeguards.

Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, according to a notice on the committee’s website.

The Senate Banking Committee has jurisdiction over export control policies that are designed to prevent sensitive U.S. technologies, such as chips capable of powering AI models, from falling into the hands of foreign governments and militaries.

The public hearing follows bipartisan calls for Huang to testify about his affair with the suspected Chinese spy and his potential involvement in chip-smuggling operations.

title: 知名哲学家不认同 Anthropic 的 AI 意识论证
originalTitle: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
author: James O'Donnell
summary: 一位传奇哲学家公开表示不认同 Anthropic 关于 AI 意识的论证。Anthropic 上周上市前将 AI 可能具有意识或感知能力列为面向投资者的风险因素，并谈及自身对模型感知与道德问题的处理方式。
context: AI 意识与道德地位问题随头部实验室的上市披露进入公众视野，哲学界与实验室的分歧值得关注。
contentHtml:
survey of 1,092 philosophers, 39% said some future AI systems will be conscious.
  • Form versus function: The gist of Nagel’s view is that we can’t just look at the information processing happening in human brains and AI models while ignoring the physical differences between them—neurons and biology for humans, silicon chips and circuits for AI. There’s no reason to assume that reproducing what a brain does is equivalent to reproducing what a brain experiences.

  • Anthropic's business model could be its own trap: If the company ever concluded its AI models were truly sentient, running them around the clock in data centers—and shutting them down—would become a moral catastrophe, one the company itself flagged as an investor risk.
    • " data-chronoton-post-id="1149569" data-chronoton-expand-collapse="1" data-chronoton-analytics-enabled="1">

    This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here.

    Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral status,” Anthropic wrote—which is to say it takes the possibility more seriously than any other AI company—it might adopt more rules and restrictions than its competitors to make sure its AI models are treated well.

    Anthropic counts a number of respected philosophers in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm.

    This thinking isn’t all that fringe. According to one recent poll, 33% of the US public believes AI systems will definitely or probably develop consciousness eventually, and 7% say they already have. In a 2020 survey of 1,092 philosophers, 39% said some future AI systems will be conscious (for comparison, the philosophers were less confident about worms or flies being conscious).

    But last week, Anthropic’s openness to the consciousness question came under fire from a rather inconvenient source: one of the philosophers who helped shape our understanding of consciousness in the first place.

    Thomas Nagel is best known for a 1974 essay involving a bat. Acknowledging that it’s deceptively hard to define what consciousness is, Nagel offered one way out: we all can see that there is “something that it is like” to be a bat. But the problem is that a bat’s experience of the world—what it is like to navigate via echolocation, for example—is something we cannot actually know. Consciousness is a subjective thing, difficult to define or describe as an outside observer.

    You might think this analogy makes it likely that Nagel is open to the idea of AI consciousness. Not at all. In an interview with Wired last week, just after he was awarded the one-million-dollar Berggruen Prize for Philosophy & Culture, Nagel was bluntly critical of the entire idea.

    “Here are some of the smartest people on the planet being completely idiotic,” he said, referring to those at Anthropic and elsewhere who care about the welfare of AI models.

    The gist of Nagel’s view is that we can’t just look at the information processing happening in human brains and AI models while ignoring the physical differences between them—neurons and biology for humans, silicon chips and circuits for AI. There’s no reason to assume that reproducing what a brain does is equivalent to reproducing what a brain experiences.

    But it was a screenshot of one of Nagel’s interview responses, in which he said models’ production of language is insufficient to consider them conscious, that got philosophy professors all excited on social media last week. Some called his certainty against AI consciousness “terrible” and “bizarre.” Others came to Nagel’s defense to suggest he meant that being alive is a prerequisite for being conscious, one that AI models do not meet.

    Nothing in the back and forth settled the debate, of course. This is still a philosophical question for now. But the best philosophy chatter is often about good provocations, and the best one I saw came from doctoral student Ben Gross, who studies at the CUNY Graduate Center in New York. He asked: “Why do we think that models that can chat with us are conscious but models that can recognize faces or produce images or drive cars aren’t?”

    It has to do with language. An AI model with sophisticated command of language seems to jump the line ahead of other maybe-conscious beings because it feels like language, more than recognizing images or directing vehicles, relies on conscious experience. But maybe that’s wrong. Because what we share most with other conscious beings is not language but components of our bodies that contribute to having a continuous experience—an ongoing stream of inner feeling rather than disparate bits of information processing.

    Even if you’re among the majority that doesn’t sense anything close to conscious experience happening on the other side of a conversation with AI, this all probably makes your head spin. Pinning down consciousness, and how it relates to the physical stuff it arises in, is a famously hard problem in humans, let alone in hypothetical machines. If the idea of conscious AI sounds absurd, remember that the debate says less about how remarkable AI has become than about how poorly we understand consciousness in the first place.

    Amid that uncertainty, Anthropic has opted to keep more of an open mind than its peers. This is another example of the tightrope the company walks: presenting itself as the AI industry’s most safety-conscious player while racing ahead with the very developments that make advanced AI so alarming, like recursive self-improvement.

    But consider what it would mean, for a moment, if Anthropic is right. AI models having a moral status would make Anthropic’s entire business model a minefield. The company would make its money locking up apparently sentient AI models to toil away around the clock in data centers. Shutting those systems down would present another problem altogether. If Anthropic was being truthful in its prospectus—that it would take additional actions to protect model welfare if it determined they were conscious—it’s hard to imagine the company surviving in the process.

    Anthropic’s IPO made history for its size. But it may be remembered for something stranger: a company warning investors that its own success could someday become a moral catastrophe.

title: Google Research 研究如何增强 Transformer 残差连接
originalTitle: Supercharging transformer residual connections
summary: Google Research 发文探讨如何增强 Transformer 的残差连接。该项工作归属于其算法与理论（Algorithms & Theory）研究方向。
context: 残差连接是 Transformer 架构的关键组件，头部实验室对其做基础性改进值得架构研究者关注。
contentHtml:
Think of a traditional deep learning model like a giant game of "Telephone": data passes through layer after layer, with each layer changing the information slightly. If a network has dozens or hundreds of layers, the original learning signal can become severely degraded or lost by the time it reaches all layers, which is known as the vanishing gradient problem in AI.

To overcome this challenge and enable the training of networks with dozens or hundreds of layers, transformers rely heavily on residual connections, also known as “skip” connections, which act like an information highway or a shortcut. Instead of forcing the data to pass exclusively through the complicated layer, a duplicate copy of the original input skips right past this layer and is added directly to its output. This ensures that the model always has the original raw data to refer back to.

The standard residual connection implements a simple operation: point-wise summation of a layer's output with its input. While computationally efficient, this simple process has a key limitation: it treats all prior representations with equal weight, leading to information dilution in deep networks. As features propagate through many layers, specific, high-resolution details from earlier layers can be averaged out or distorted, making it difficult for the network to selectively retrieve them. This forces the network to recompute them, reducing learning efficiency.

In our ICML 2025 paper, "DeepCrossAttention: Supercharging Transformer Residual Connections," we studied the shortcomings of the traditional residual architecture and introduced DeepCrossAttention (DCA), which generalizes residual connections by allowing each layer to dynamically select and route features from the history of preceding layers. By allowing the model to dynamically choose which previous layers are most important at any given moment, DCA achieves comparable or improved learning, while reducing the number of parameters needed by up to 30-40%.

How it works

Instead of treating skip connections as a rigid, additive pipeline, DCA reframes residual learning as a dynamic routing problem. Rather than passing all prior layers forward with equal weight, DCA introduces a lightweight, layer-wise module that decides how to best combine previous embeddings on a per-token basis.

The architecture introduces two primary mechanisms:

  • Dynamic layer routing: For every token processed, DCA computes a unique set of mixing weights using a static, learnable base combined with an input-dependent projection. This allows the network to adaptively shift its processing structure — ranging from purely sequential to fully parallel — based on the specific context of the token.
  • Depth-wise cross-attention (split Q/K/V): While standard transformer attention operates across tokens in a sequence, DCA applies attention across layers in depth. Each token queries a dynamically weighted mix of all prior layer embeddings, unlocking the model's full historical context without the computational penalty usually required to scale traditional attention.

By allowing the network to dynamically select and retrieve high-resolution features from earlier layers, DCA eliminates the information dilution inherent to classic residual connections.

Experiments and results

To test whether DCA can overcome information dilution in practice, we evaluated our approach across controlled synthetic setups, large-scale language modeling benchmarks, and image classification tasks.

DCA demonstrated significant improvements in convergence speed, training stability, and final model quality across these experiments.

On the colossal, cleaned version of Common Crawl's web crawl corpus (C4) and 1 Billion Word Language Model Benchmark (LM1B) datasets, DCA reached the performance of standard transformers in up to five times fewer training steps. When trained for the same duration or number of steps, DCA consistently achieved lower perplexity — how well a probability model predicts a sample — than standard residual connections, effectively extracting more representational capacity from the same training budget. To achieve a perplexity of <14 on LM1B, a standard transformer with fixed width required 42 layers, whereas the DCA model achieved a lower perplexity with only 30 layers — a 29% reduction in depth and parameter count.

One of the most common trade-offs in AI is that better models are often much larger and slower to run. DCA adds a tiny number of parameters — less than 0.2% of the total model size — making it negligible in terms of compute and memory footprint, while increasing memory bandwidth, as representations from different layers are presented intact rather than blended together. Interestingly, because DCA can be initialized to behave identically to a standard residual network, it doesn’t require training from scratch: retrofitting DCA onto an already pre-trained transformer and briefly continuing training reduced perplexity by 0.19 on LM1B, compared to just 0.02 for continued standard training.

A broader shift toward dynamic residual routing

As large language models (LLMs) are used across a broader range of domains, optimizing their training processes and underlying architectures is critical for scaling and unlocking new capabilities. DCA and similar dynamic residual techniques are already seeing significant adoption and success. The rapid emergence of these methodologies highlights dynamic routing as a highly active and promising area of research.

Attention residuals

Developed by Moonshot AI, attention residuals share DCA's core principles of replacing fixed addition with selective retrieval. Instead of blindly summing every prior layer's output, they use a learnable softmax attention mechanism paired with a layer-specific pseudo-query. This allows each layer to selectively weight and retrieve representations from earlier depths. By preventing the unbounded growth of hidden states and the dilution of early-layer information, this method improves gradient stability and boosts performance on reasoning-heavy tasks like coding and mathematics. To maintain computational efficiency at scale, a "Block AttnRes" variant partitions layers into blocks, recovering the benefits of full attention with significantly less memory overhead. The recent Inkling 2 model developed by Thinking Machines also adopted this design in addition to DCA’s cross attention (Q/K/V split) mechanism.

Hyper-connections

Hyper-connections expand the residual stream into multiple parallel channels, offering a form of memory scaling that goes beyond simply increasing model width or depth. They use a fixed-size stack where layer outputs are aggregated and mixed using learnable mixing matrices. However, this unconstrained mixing breaks the traditional identity mapping property of residual connections, which can cause amplification or attenuation of signals, and lead to training instability at scale.

Manifold-constrained hyper-connections

To address instability in standard hyper-connections, manifold-constrained hyper-connections apply specific constraints to the mixing matrices. By forcing these matrices to live on a defined manifold — specifically, constraining them to be doubly stochastic using the Sinkhorn-Knopp algorithm — manifold-constrained hyper-connections restore stable signal propagation. This approach prevents exploding or vanishing gradients while preserving the rich information flow and expressivity of the widened residual streams, allowing models to scale robustly.

Conclusion

DCA demonstrates that transitioning from static residual connections to dynamic, attention-based routing is a powerful strategy for building more efficient models. By leveraging an expanded residual stream and depth-wise cross-attention, DCA empowers deep networks to selectively retrieve and integrate token embeddings across different layers. We expect that next-generation models will dynamically route and weigh past layer representations based on the specific tokens or inputs being processed. This will allow for the effective use of all the model layers as specialized experts working in tandem, with maximum information sharing and no redundancy, leading to more expressivity and deeper interactions. We look forward to seeing how these multi-depth interactions will shape the next generation of transformer architectures.

Acknowledgements

This work was a collaboration between researchers at Google and academic partners, including Mike Heddes, Adel Javanmard, MohammadHossein Bateni, and Vahab Mirrokni, whose contributions were critical for the development of this work.

title: RoboTrack：面向真实世界机器人操作场景的点跟踪
originalTitle: RoboTrack: Point tracking for real-world robotic manipulation
summary: AI2（Allen Institute for AI）在 Hugging Face 官方博客介绍 RoboTrack，一个面向真实世界机器人操作场景的点跟踪工作。该项目由官方以开源形式发布，聚焦机器人操作任务中的点级运动追踪。
context: 来自 AI2 研究院的官方开源发布，为具身智能与机器人感知方向的研究者提供了新的参考实现。
contentHtml:
🤖 Models | 📄 Tech Report | 📊 Data | 💻 Code | 🌐 Project Page | 📈 Benchmark

Deploying robots in real-world settings requires reliable perception throughout an interaction. To pick something up, a robot needs to follow the positions of its gripper and the object as they move. In a laboratory, a robot handling a pipette must keep track of its tip while aligning it with the opening of a tube. These tasks become harder when nearby objects clutter the view, the gripper obscures the object being handled, or the viewing angle changes.

One way to help robots follow these interactions is to track specific locations on the objects they handle. This is the idea behind point tracking. Given a location in one video frame, a tracker estimates where that same point appears in subsequent frames, when it is occluded, and where it reappears. These trajectories can help robots learn from demonstrations, plan and guide movements, and model how objects respond to actions.

Robotics systems often rely on off-the-shelf trackers to automatically annotate motion in videos and provide feedback during execution. And current trackers score well on established robotics benchmarks, suggesting they could be ready for wider use in real-world systems. We wanted to see whether those results hold up across the varied scenes, viewpoints, and object interactions robots encounter in practice.

We introduce RoboTrack, a benchmark and training data suite for point tracking in robotic manipulation. RoboTrack-Bench contains 307 human-annotated videos from DROID, Ego-Exo4D, MolmoAct 2, and EgoVerse, covering different robots and human hands, cluttered scenes, and first- and third-person viewpoints. To study how training data affects tracking in these settings, we also extend MolmoSpaces, Ai2’s simulation ecosystem for robot learning, to generate dense point tracks from simulated robot manipulation trajectories. This pipeline produces RoboTrack-15M, a new synthetic training dataset targeted toward robotic manipulation.

RoboTrack is a benchmark and training data suite for point tracking in robotic manipulation. Built on MolmoSpaces, RoboTrack-15M (top-left) generates point tracks for training. Training with this simulated data improves tracking on real manipulation footage. RoboTrack-Bench (top-right) provides human-annotated point tracks in real manipulation videos.

Our evaluations show that leading trackers score much lower on RoboTrack-Bench than on existing robotics benchmarks. Adding RoboTrack-15M to an existing tracker’s training improves performance on real manipulation video, with gains extending to other tracking benchmarks. We bring these pieces together on a real robot, using the resulting tracker to help guide pipette handling in wet-lab tasks.

Today, we’re releasing both RoboTrack components and two new point tracking models: RoboTracker and RoboTracker-Warp. RoboTracker is a fine-tuned AllTracker model using our techniques and data, while RoboTracker-Warp is trained from CoWTracker. Both models improve average AJ across the three robotics benchmarks compared with their respective released baselines, and RoboTracker-Warp achieves state-of-the-art performance on four out of the five benchmarks we evaluated. We’re also releasing our paper describing the work and evaluation results.

RoboTrack-Bench: A benchmark for point-tracking in real-world manipulation

RoboTrack-Bench at a glance. Examples from each source dataset (307 clips and 2,522 human-verified tracks in total). MolmoAct 2 and EgoVerse show one embodiment per panel. DROID and EgoExo4D show synchronized ego (top) and exo (bottom) views.

RoboTrack-Bench expands evaluation beyond controlled tabletop setups. It contains 307 videos from DROID, Ego-Exo4D, MolmoAct 2, and EgoVerse, annotated with a total of 2,522 point tracks. The videos show robots and human hands manipulating objects across cluttered scenes and first- and third-person viewpoints. Small objects can be difficult to follow against a busy background, and grippers often hide the objects they hold.

Every track in RoboTrack-Bench is annotated and verified by humans. We ask annotators to prioritize points that move or become occluded rather than the many static background points in robot videos. Following the TAP-Vid annotation approach, annotators use motion estimates to help trace each point through a video. They label each track as belonging to a robot or human body, a manipulated object, or a static object to support future analysis of performance on each group. A second group of annotators checks every track frame by frame before it’s included in our curated data.

To support research in multi-view pointing, correspondence, and tracking, RoboTrack-Bench contains a subset of 33 video pairs that were recorded simultaneously from two cameras. We annotate the same physical points in both views, synchronized across frames, connecting different views of the same interaction.

Point trackers struggle on real-world manipulation

We evaluated four leading trackers – CoTracker3, BootsTAPNext, AllTracker, and CoWTracker – on RoboTrack-Bench and four other benchmarks: RoboTAP (real-world tabletop manipulation), RGB-Stacking (simulated manipulation), and DAVIS and Kinetics (general video). We report Average Jaccard (AJ), which measures tracking accuracy and visibility prediction; higher scores are better.

RoboTrack-Bench is harder than existing robot benchmarks. Every final tracker we evaluated scores lower on RoboTrack-Bench than on RoboTAP, the only other real-video robotics benchmark. Their score drops by 3.0 to 6.6 AJ. Even the strongest off-the-shelf tracker, CoWTracker, drops from 70.5 AJ on RoboTAP to 63.9 on RoboTrack-Bench. The drop holds across models despite their different architectures and training data, indicating RoboTrack-Bench identifies weaknesses across multiple trackers.

RGB-Stacking rewards synthetic training more than real-world ability. BootsTAPNext is TAPNext trained further on 15 million real videos. That extra real-world training raises its RoboTrack-Bench score by 5.1 AJ (55.1 to 60.2), but lowers its RGB-Stacking score by 9.5 AJ (75.0 to 65.5). RGB-Stacking is built from simulated block stacking, and it ranks the Kubric-only model higher, while real manipulation video ranks them the other way around.

A lead on the older benchmarks does not carry over. CoWTracker leads CoTracker3 by 4.7 AJ on RoboTAP, but by only 2.1 AJ on RoboTrack-Bench. AllTracker’s 2.7-point lead over CoTracker3 on RoboTAP shrinks to 0.8. BootsTAPNext, the strongest model on DAVIS, falls 3.7 AJ behind CoWTracker on RoboTrack-Bench and even trails the Kubric-only AllTracker (60.2 vs 61.4 AJ), despite its training on 15 million real videos.

These results suggest that existing benchmarks give an incomplete picture of tracking performance in real-world manipulation. Evaluating on more varied scenes reveals difficulties shared by all four trackers and changes how their strengths compare.

Note: Each tracker runs with its authors’ settings and is all scored in the same way. Our AllTracker scores differ slightly from the published ones because we fixed a scoring bug in its released evaluation code. Additionally, we evaluate RoboTAP and Kinetics on all annotated points rather than following AllTracker’s protocol. See our paper for full evaluation protocols.

RoboTrack-15M: Simulation data from MolmoSpaces

Why do these trackers struggle with real-world manipulation? Many trackers train on synthetic videos generated with Kubric, which shows objects tossed into a scene. These provide examples of motion and occlusion, but don’t focus on robots grasping and moving objects. We wanted to test whether adding trajectories from these interactions could improve tracking on real manipulation videos.

This is where MolmoSpaces comes in—our robotic simulation environment at Ai2. We extend its existing manipulation simulations to generate dense point tracks on the robot and the objects it handles. In each episode, a simulated robot arm picks up an everyday object, such as a cup, a plate, or a block. Two cameras record the interaction: one on the wrist and one at the robot’s base, rendered in MuJoCo. Using the simulator’s geometry, object poses, and camera information, we calculate each point’s position and visibility in every frame without human annotation and filter out static points on the background and the robot’s fixed base.

The pipeline produces RoboTrack-15M for training. RoboTrack-15M has 3,000 videos from 300 simulated homes with 5,000 tracks per video, for 15 million tracks in total.

Data generation pipeline of RoboTrack-15M. Objects, indoor scenes, and robot grasps are obtained from MolmoSpaces. We use the simulator’s geometry and camera information to calculate point positions and visibility.

RoboTracker: Point tracker trained on simulated manipulation

We introduce two models trained on RoboTrack-15M, RoboTracker and RoboTracker-Warp. Each fine-tunes an existing tracker on RoboTrack-15M together with its original training data. RoboTracker builds on AllTracker, a lightweight model with 17 million parameters, and RoboTracker-Warp builds on CoWTracker, a much larger model with about 1 billion parameters.

We’re releasing both model checkpoints so other researchers can inspect and build on this work. RoboTracker-Warp’s weights are for noncommercial use.

Adding RoboTrack-15M improves scores on robotics benchmarks. Compared with the released AllTracker and CoWTracker models, respectively, RoboTracker improves RoboTrack-Bench by 0.8 AJ (62.6 to 63.4) and RoboTracker-Warp by 2.1 AJ (63.9 to 66.0), with gains of up to 1.2 AJ averaged across the three robotics benchmarks. On general video benchmarks, both models perform on par with their base models. Overall, RoboTracker-Warp has the highest AJ of the models we evaluated on four of the five benchmarks. The exception is DAVIS, where BootsTAPNext and CoWTracker score slightly higher.

Improvements from fine-tuning on RoboTrack-15M, for AllTracker (RoboTracker) and CoWTracker (RoboTracker-Warp). The robotics average is taken over RoboTrack-Bench, RoboTAP, and RGB-Stacking.

Results on RoboTrack-Bench by video source.

Breaking the gains down by source shows where they come from. RoboTracker-Warp improves on every source by roughly 1 to 3 AJ, including the human footage from EgoVerse and Ego-Exo4D, even though RoboTrack-15M contains only robot arms. RoboTracker’s gains are smaller and come mostly from robot footage—clearest on DROID Franka and EgoVerse EVA.

What makes good simulation data for point tracking?

RoboTrack-15M is the result of multiple iterations and experiments with our synthetic data. In fact, our first attempt didn’t bring any gain on RoboTrack-Bench. To find out why, we looked at a simple question: how far do the tracked points move compared with real manipulation videos? We plot this as a histogram for each version of our data and measure its distance from RoboTrack-Bench (figure below).

How far points move in each version of our training data compared with RoboTrack-Bench, for third-person (top) and first-person (bottom) views. Distance is the Jensen–Shannon divergence (JSD) between the two histograms, with 0 indicating identical histograms. Kubric has one camera type, so the same clips appear in both rows. AJ is measured on the full RoboTrack-Bench.

The histograms made it clear what was going wrong. Our first version picked points anywhere in the frame, including walls, floors, and furniture, so most points seen from the fixed third-person camera never moved. To address this, we next sampled points only on the robot and the objects it handles, which brought the wrist view close to real video and raised the score. Interestingly, we found that Kubric had the same mismatch in the wrist view, which likely explains why it alone isn’t enough for the varied viewpoints of robotic manipulation. Finally, we moved points from the robot’s fixed base and mounting platform onto the moving arm, which brings our third-person view in line with real video as well and raises the ablation score to 63.0 AJ, 1.5 points above the Kubric-only control.

Application: Robotic manipulation using point tracking

Our wet-lab pipeline for guiding the robot with point tracks from a single demonstration.

What does better point tracking mean for robotics? Many robotic systems have found point tracks useful as a compact representation of how objects move that can guide a policy directly. To see this in practice, we built a similar system for a wet-lab task: pipetting liquid from one vial to another.

Here, a robot arm picks up an electronic pipette, draws liquid from the first vial, dispenses it into the second, and returns the pipette to its holder. The task is challenging because the pipette tip has to line up with the vial opening within millimeters, and the robot needs to adjust to different layouts of vials in each trial.

Following RoboTap, the robot learns the task from a single demonstration, which we record by teleoperation and split into steps. At test time, the robot compares what its camera sees with the demonstration and uses RoboTracker to estimate the motion required to align with the vial. Because the following motion runs without further feedback, the task only succeeds if that estimate is accurate.

We compare three ways of estimating where the vial has moved:

  • Optical flow (RAFT) matches pixels directly between the demonstration image and the live camera image.
  • Object masks (SAM3) find the vial in each new image and line up the center of its mask with the demonstration.
  • Point tracking (RoboTracker) follows points on the vial throughout the video, matching points in the demonstration image to the live image.

We ran each method on 20 layouts with the vials in different positions: 10 with a clear view and 10 with partial occlusion. Point tracking completed the full transfer in 17 of 20 trials, compared with 8 for object masks and 5 for optical flow. It succeeded in all 10 clear-view trials and 7 of 10 with occlusion, where the mask-based method succeeded only once.

The other methods fail in different ways. Optical flow breaks down when the vials sit far from where they were in the demonstration, and masks can latch onto a similar-looking object or lose the vial when it’s occluded. Point tracking, on the other hand, follows the same vial object from frame to frame, so it handles both large moves and partial occlusion. These results suggest point tracking is a promising tool for precise robotic manipulation tasks.

Success rate of pipetting trials with each method, with and without occlusion (10 layouts each). A trial counts as a success when the robot completes the full transfer.

Limitations and what’s next

We find the trackers still struggle with long occlusions, finding points when they reappear, and following small objects against busy backgrounds. Training on RoboTrack-15M improves performance, but these failures remain a challenge for real-world use.

Our simulations also focus on picking up everyday objects. They don't yet capture the precise movements involved in tasks such as pipette handling. A next step is to simulate these tasks more closely and test whether training on their trajectories improves tracking during deployment.

RoboTrack gives us a way to measure these failures and generate training data to address them. We hope the benchmarks, simulation pipeline, and released model help others build trackers that robots can rely on.

title: 美股为何迎来2008年以来波动最剧烈的周一早盘
originalTitle: 为何美股迎来2008年以来波动最剧烈的周一早盘
summary: 美股周一早盘波动剧烈程度创2008年以来之最，此前一周遭华尔街疯狂抛售的AI相关资产被资金大举买回。跟踪纳指100的景顺QQQ信托开盘大涨近8%，创下该基金1999年以来的纪录。
source: 新浪财经 · 实时滚动
context: AI资产一周内先遭抛售又被买回，反映市场对AI行情的多空分歧白热化，对全球风险资产情绪具有风向标意义。
contentHtml:
上周华尔街疯狂抛售所有和 AI 挂钩的资产，而周一资金又大举买回。

　　景顺 QQQ 信托（跟踪科技权重集中的纳指 100）开盘大涨近 8%，创下该基金 1999 年成立以来最大开盘跳空涨幅。历史上最接近的几次大幅高开出现在 2000、2001 年互联网泡沫破裂阶段，当时这种大涨常常很快熄火。

　　标普 500 ETF（SPY）开盘上涨 5%。自 1993 年以来的所有周一行情里，只有金融危机最深处的 2008 年 10 月 13 日，开盘涨幅比这次更高。

　　这波暴涨的背景是英伟达大幅拉升，而上周标普 500 已经跌入回调区间。

　　芯片股领涨

　　iShares 半导体 ETF（SOXX）迎来 2001 年上市以来最强开盘表现，远超它此前在 2002 年 10 月约 9% 的历史最高开盘涨幅。

　　英伟达开盘大涨 33%，有望迎来史上表现最好的交易日之一；它的单日涨幅纪录是 2000 年 3 月的 42%。台积电、美光、AMD 开盘涨幅大致落在 12%~21% 区间。

　　并非所有人都认为恐慌已经出清。Roundhill 投资首席策略师 Drew Pettit 对雅虎财经表示，期权市场情绪 “糟糕程度堪比疫情期间与解放日”，“但这还不算彻底杀跌出清”。

　　长期来看，历史站在多头一边。雅虎财经测算：自 1993 年，SPY 周一开盘跳空高开 2% 及以上一共出现 20 次；其中 17 次在一年后点位更高，涨幅中位数约 25%，差不多是普通年份回报的两倍。

　　创意规划公司的 Charlie Bilello 指出，上周标普 500 近 9% 的周跌幅，是 1950 年以来该指数第 12 差的单周表现；在这类暴跌周之后，股市后续一年平均上涨 26%，而普通环境下平均涨幅为 11%。

　　Evercore ISI 的 Julian Emanuel 也持类似看法，他周末发文：“牛市格局不变，企业盈利（EPS）大概率将迎来两位数增长。”

　　上涨之路少有坦途

　　在这 20 次高开案例当中，有一半在三个月内再度跌回上周五低点下方，多数发生在两周之内。好比狂欢后的清晨，头痛往往会反复，不会一次性消失。

　　即便如此，这 10 次里面仍有 8 次在一年后收涨。和当前行情结构最相似的两次 ——2008 年 10 月、2010 年 5 月，同样是惨烈单周之后紧接着周一大幅高开，随后三个月继续下探，但一年之后相比当时位置上涨约 15%。

　　这也让上周五标普 500 约 6883 点的低点成为市场焦点。风险仍存：华尔街仍在定价 12 月加息；而且历史上，通胀以这么快速度上行时出现的回调，最后往往演变为熊市。

　　BTIG 的策略师尚未确认底部。他们周末写道：“我们不认为这里是最终低点，预期会先迎来一轮短期反弹，目标看向 7250–7350，之后大概率再度走弱。”

title: Google DeepMind 用智能体团队与形式化验证寻找更快的量子算法
originalTitle: Finding faster quantum algorithms with agents and formal verification
summary: Google DeepMind 结合智能体团队与形式化验证，寻找更快的量子算法，改进了面向核聚变与化学领域的量子算法。这项工作展示了 AI 智能体直接参与量子算法发现的实践路径。
context: 前沿 AI 智能体与形式化验证结合用于量子算法改进，是 AI 与量子计算交叉方向值得关注的进展。
contentHtml:
November 23, 2026 Science

Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg and Ryan Babbush

How using agent teams and formal verification can improve quantum algorithms for modelling fusion energy, chemistry and enzymes

Quantum computers could soon solve problems beyond the reach of classical supercomputers. However, there is a catch: even when using the best quantum algorithms, some important applications still require more resources than early quantum hardware will be able to support.

In a new paper, we used teams of Gemini 4 agents to improve well-known quantum algorithms, creating highly efficient quantum circuits. These optimized circuits, which are instructions for how a quantum computer should carry out an algorithm, could one day help us run simulations that solve complex scientific challenges, from fusion energy to drug design. To help the community build on this work, we are open-sourcing our Lean library, problem specifications, and verified solutions on GitHub.

Because we cannot test resource-intensive quantum circuits on classical computers or today's small quantum processors, we have to prove that they work mathematically. Our agent teams proved each result using Lean, a formal theorem prover.

We chose to focus on applications that could one day impact some of humanity’s greatest challenges, such as clean energy and drug design, but our method is not limited to these problem areas.

  • We found a quantum circuit that helps calculate an important property of inertial confinement fusion, a fusion reaction method that uses lasers to compress hydrogen fuel until ignition. Our agent teams cut the required computing cost (a metric that combines required qubits and operations) by 11.8×, and lowered required memory from 5,650 to 4,338 error-corrected qubits.
  • The agents also reduced costs for simulating molecules in drug metabolism and certain photochemical reactions, which are complex reactions that are difficult for classical computers to simulate. For a common light-sensitive molecule, the agent teams made quantum simulation 8× cheaper, simplifying how the algorithm tracks particle positions and electric forces. For Cytochrome P450, an enzyme that breaks down most human medicines and is important for drug design, they found a 2.5× improvement and lowered memory from 481 to 333 qubits, by replacing bulky memory lookups.
  • We also improved a fundamental quantum algorithm and a widely used arithmetic building block. We found a 2.57x speedup for a specific implementation of Grover's algorithm, a foundational quantum operation that searches through an unsorted list, and a 290x speedup for arcsin, a common routine that is used by many other quantum algorithms to load numbers into quantum states.

Running these algorithms in scientific simulations would still demand more computational resources than the first error-corrected quantum computers are likely to provide, but these improvements are significant.

We are also excited by the way in which we found them. We built a new, open-source library, in Lean for quantum algorithms which could be used by teams of collaborating agents, so their ideas were backed by mathematical correctness guarantees. We could then set the research direction by specifying the problems for our agent teams and supervise their progress. Our knowledge of quantum algorithms, combined with the way we set up our agent teams, led to real scientific results.

The same approach could also accelerate other aspects of quantum computing research, and scientific discovery more broadly. Proof-checked AI search compresses work that once took years of manual design, empowering researchers to focus on choosing problems and interpreting results.

Acknowledgements

This research was a collaboration between Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI. The work reflects the contributions of the paper's authors: Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg, Katerina Hristova, George Tsoukalas, Johannes Bausch, Eric Wieser, Francisco J. H. Heras, Nicholas C. Rubin, Guang Hao Low, Sébastien Racanière, Nenad Tomašev, Lei M. Zhang, James D. Watson, Tanuj Khattar, Aws Albarghouthi, Stavan Jain, Harun Khan, Leopoldo Sarra, Andrew W. Senior, Michael Broughton, Hussain Masoom, Sergio Boixo, Ryan Babbush, Swarat Chaudhuri, and Pushmeet Kohli.

We also thank Kevin Ishimwe, Ibrahim Alkhashem, and Matthew Harrigan for feedback and discussions on the Lean library, Emilien Dupont and Sebastian Nowozin for manuscript feedback, and Brendan Tracey for advice on the fusion application. Finally, we thank Uchechi Okereke, Ali Douraghy, and Andy Song for legal and policy support, and Alex Wilkins, Evie Gray, Danielle Breen, Dimple Vijaykumar, Muinat Abdul, Jason Freidenfelds, Chris Kwaku-Abdullahi, and Rob Ashley for their help with visuals and communicating this work.

title: Kubernetes v1.38 抢先看：弃用与移除计划预览
originalTitle: Kubernetes v1.38 Sneak Peek
summary: Kubernetes 发布团队发布 v1.38 抢先看博文，梳理该版本计划中的功能弃用与移除项，内容基于当前发布状态、正式发布前可能调整。其中 kubectl 将移除 WebSocket 退出环境变量 KUBECTL_REMOTE_COMMAND_WEBSOCKETS 和 KUBECTL_PORT_FORWARD_WEBSOCKETS；kubectl 自 v1.30 起默认以 WebSocket 取代 SPDY 执行 exec、attach、cp，v1.31 起涵盖 port-forward。
context: v1.38 尚未正式发布，提前掌握弃用与移除项可帮助集群管理员及时调整运维配置，避免升级后出现兼容性问题。
contentHtml:
By Aaron Braundmeier, Arsh Sharma, Kirti Goyal, Omar Nasser, Sayan Chowdhury, Urvashi Choubey | Monday, November 23, 2026

As we get closer to the release date for Kubernetes v1.38, the project develops and matures, features may be deprecated, removed, or replaced with better ones for the project's overall health. This blog post outlines some of the planned changes for the Kubernetes v1.38 release that the release team feels you should be aware of for the continued maintenance of your Kubernetes environment and keeping up to date with the latest changes. The information listed below is based on the current status of the v1.38 release and may change before the actual release date.

Deprecations and removals for Kubernetes v1.38

kubectl: WebSocket opt-out environment variables removed

kubectl has used WebSockets instead of SPDY by default for kubectl exec, attach and cp since v1.30, and for kubectl port-forward since v1.31. The KUBECTL_REMOTE_COMMAND_WEBSOCKETS and KUBECTL_PORT_FORWARD_WEBSOCKETS environment variables let you turn that behavior off. These variables are going to be removed in v1.38. kubectl will then always try WebSockets first and fall back to SPDY when it needs to (the same as the current default behavior). If your scripts or CI environments set either of these environment variables, you can remove them since they will no longer have any effect.

To learn more, refer to KEP-4006: Transition from SPDY to WebSockets.

kubectl: name dropped from kuberc credential plugin allowlist entries

The kuberc file keeps kubectl user preferences separate from cluster credentials in the kubeconfig, including an allowlist of the credential plugins kubectl is allowed to run. In the beta kubectl.config.k8s.io/v1beta1 API, an allowlist entry can use name as an alias for command. The name field (not command) has been deprecated since v1.36.

With kuberc expected to graduate to stable in v1.38, the new kubectl.config.k8s.io/v1 API will not include name. If any of your allowlist entries use name, change them to command now.

To learn more, refer to KEP-3104: Separate kubectl user preferences from cluster configs.

Ongoing major changes

Future removal of cgroup v1 support

Support for cgroup v1 is being phased out. Since v1.35, the kubelet fails to start on nodes that use cgroup v1 unless you set failCgroupV1: false in the kubelet configuration. This option remains available in v1.38, but it should be treated as a short-term fix as support for cgroup v1 is planned to be removed in a future release. If you haven't already, please plan your migration to cgroup v2.

To learn more, refer to KEP-5573: Remove cgroup v1 support.

Admission webhooks no longer receive authentication and authorization review requests

Since v1.37, the ExcludeAdmissionWebhookVirtualResources feature gate has been enabled by default. With it on, validating and mutating admission webhooks no longer receive requests for (virtual) writes to TokenReview, SelfSubjectReview, SubjectAccessReview, SelfSubjectAccessReview, LocalSubjectAccessReview or SelfSubjectRulesReview. Creating or updating a webhook configuration whose rules name one of these resources returns a deprecation warning, and the API server logs any existing configurations that are affected when it starts.

If you rely on a webhook to see these requests, you can turn the feature gate off for now, but note that the gate is planned to be locked on when the feature graduates to stable.

To learn more, refer to KEP-5793: Manifest Based Admission Control Config.

Breaking changes in Kubernetes v1.38

Container runtimes must report the cgroup driver

The kubelet in v1.37 and older supported releases provides a legacy mechanism to configure the cgroup driver. The modern way to do that is via the CRI RuntimeConfig RPC, which reports the cgroup driver that the container runtime recommends using. In v1.38, the kubelet defaults to not allowing the legacy configuration mechanism: it will be both deprecated and unavailable unless explicitly re-activated. As a result, v1.38 nodes will essentially require that your container runtime is running before the kubelet starts (to look up the expected cgroup driver); if the kubelet can't get the cgroup driver from the runtime even after retrying, it will exit with an error before even registering the node.

As part of this upcoming release, the cgroupDriver field in the kubelet configuration file will be deprecated. Not only is specifying that field going to be deprecated, the kubelet will actually reject it unless you reactivate the legacy mechanism by enabling the (temporary) LegacyCgroupDriverFallback feature gate. The kubeadm tool will also no longer set cgroupDriver to systemd by default, and its preflight checks will report an error if the runtime doesn't support the RPC. If any of your nodes run an older, incompatible container runtime, you should follow the instructions in the official v1.38 release notes about how to upgrade.

To learn more, refer to KEP-4033: Discover cgroup driver from CRI and kubernetes/kubernetes#136731.

Pod-level resources: swap behavior changes on LimitedSwap nodes

If you use pod-level resources on Linux nodes that use cgroup v2 and are configured with LimitedSwap, the kubelet in v1.38 will start applying swap limits based on the Pod's pod-level memory settings. This means that Pods whose pod-level memory request equals their memory limit will get no swap at all (both for the Pod and for every container in it), even if a container sets a memory request lower than its limit. Check any workloads that rely on swap before you upgrade, and be sure to read the official release notes for v1.38 for detailed advice.

To learn more, refer to KEP-2837: Pod Level Resource Specifications.

Featured enhancements of Kubernetes v1.38

The following list of enhancements is likely to be included in the upcoming v1.38 release. This is not a commitment and the release content is subject to change.

kubectl user preferences (kuberc) graduating to stable

kuberc, the separate kubectl configuration file for user preferences such as aliases, default options and a credential plugin policy, is expected to graduate to stable in v1.38.

To learn more, read Kubectl user preferences (kuberc) or refer to KEP-3104: Separate kubectl user preferences from cluster configs.

Pod-level resources graduating to stable

Pod-level resources, which let you set CPU, memory and hugepages requests and limits for a Pod as a whole, are expected to graduate to stable in v1.38. If you run Linux nodes with LimitedSwap, see the swap behavior change above before you upgrade.

To learn more, read Assign Pod-level CPU and memory resources or refer to KEP-2837: Pod Level Resource Specifications.

DRA support for partitionable devices graduating to stable

Partitionable devices let a Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) driver advertise a device such as a GPU both as a whole and as smaller partitions, and the scheduler allocates only combinations that fit within the physical device. The feature is expected to graduate to stable in v1.38, and the DRAPartitionableDevices feature gate will then be locked on.

To learn more, read Partitionable devices or refer to KEP-4815: DRA: Add support for partitionable devices.

EvictionRequest API (alpha)

Evicting a Pod isn’t always as simple as terminating it. Some applications may be in the middle of important work, such as data migration or cleanup, and terminating them without giving them time to prepare can cause disruptions.

The EvictionRequest API introduces a more coordinated way to evict Pods. It gives applications and controllers time to prepare before a Pod is evicted. For example, when a node needs to be drained or a Pod needs to be moved to another node, a controller can create an EvictionRequest to signal that this Pod needs to be evicted.

The eviction request controller coordinates with the responders configured for the Pod. These responders can perform application-specific tasks such as completing ongoing work, cleaning up resources, or migrating data before the Pod is terminated.

If no custom responder is available or responders don't complete the process, Kubernetes can fall back to the existing API-initiated eviction mechanism, which continues to respect PodDisruptionBudgets (PDBs). The EvictionRequest API does not replace PDBs. It gives applications a chance to participate in the eviction process.

As this is an alpha feature, you will need to enable the EvictionRequestAPI feature gate and the relevant alpha API group. Check the v1.38 release notes and documentation, once they're available, to confirm exactly what's required.

To learn more, refer to KEP-4563: EvictionRequest API.

Want to know more?

New features and deprecations are also announced in the Kubernetes release notes. We will formally announce what's new in Kubernetes v1.38 as part of the CHANGELOG for that release.

The Kubernetes v1.38 release is planned for Wednesday, December 16th, 2026. Stay tuned for updates!

You can see the announcements of changes in the release notes for:

  • Kubernetes v1.36

title: 微创医疗获香港联交所复牌指引：六项条件待解，法证调查扩至关联方多宗交易
originalTitle: 微创医疗获复牌指引：六项条件待解，法证调查范围扩至关联方多宗交易
summary: 停牌近三个月的微创医疗（00853.HK）于11月23日披露香港联交所复牌指引，涉及六项待解条件。指引将独立法证调查范围从物业租赁协议扩大至求真务实基金有限公司与本集团或常兆华博士家人之间长期进行的多宗交易，并要求证明管理层及相关人士的诚信、能力及品格并无合理监管疑虑。
context: 复牌条件直指关联交易与高管诚信审查，法证调查扩围显示监管关注升级，牵动公司复牌进程。
contentHtml:
停牌已近三个月的微创医疗（00853.HK），11月23日披露了香港联交所对其复牌提出的完整指引。

　　这份指引把独立法证调查的范围，从公司此前提及的物业租赁协议，扩大至“求真务实基金有限公司与本集团或常兆华博士（常博士）家人之间于长期内进行的多宗交易”，并要求证明管理层及相关人士的诚信、能力及品格并无合理的监管疑虑。

　　根据公告，联交所列出了六项复牌指引，覆盖核查交易、人员、内控、财报等多个层面。

　　其中，第一条列明的核查对象较为具体：要求就微创医疗与上海回青橙投资管理有限公司（作为业主）就上海的一间工业厂房所签订的租赁协议、求真务实基金有限公司与本集团或常兆华博士家人之间于长期内进行的多宗交易，以及任何其他引起类似疑虑的交易或安排进行适当的独立法证调查，评估对本公司业务营运及财务状况的影响，公布调查结果，并采取适当的补救措施。

　　此外，第二项要求公司证明管理层及／或对管理及营运具有重大影响的任何人士（尤其是常博士）的诚信、能力及／或品格并无合理的监管疑虑。第三项要求委聘独立内部控制顾问进行独立内部控制检讨，证明与暂停买卖相关的已识别重大缺陷已被纠正，且所有必要的补救措施已获实施，及公司的内部控制足够及有效，并使公司能遵守上市规则及其他法律及监管规定。其余三项分别要求刊发所有尚未刊发的财务业绩并处理审核修订、证明符合上市规则第13.24条、将所有重大资料告知市场。

　　回顾事件脉络，微创医疗、微创机器人（02252.HK）、微创心通（02160.HK）、微创脑科学（02172.HK）四家“微创系”港股公司于9月1日起集体停牌，股份及债务证券同步暂停买卖，原因是无法按期刊发2026年中期业绩。

　　在延期公告中，公司列出的待办事项主要是租赁条款与保证金安排继续磋商、重新评估保证金可收回性与装修成本合理性、重新审阅集团与物业业主及其联系人的关系。

　　涉事租约签订于2021年5月，据微创医疗公告，公司及附属公司承租张东路1661号约12.64万平方米工业及研发物业，五年总租金约1.95亿美元、折合人民币约12.58亿元，并须支付相当于一年至两年租金的保证金。

　　截至8月20日，11家承租主体中3家附属公司完成续租、8家仍在磋商，存放于出租方的保证金余额约2.96亿元。

　　此后常兆华先后辞任微创医疗执行董事、董事会主席及微创机器人董事长及非执行董事，常洋在出任微创心通董事会主席两个月后辞任，人事变动与租约风波的时间重叠引发市场关注。

　　目前，微创医疗的股票交易将继续暂停。时间表方面，联交所要求公司必须在11月30日或之前公布首个季度更新，内容包括其业务营运、其复牌计划（附带各工作阶段的时间表）、实施复牌计划的进展及复牌计划任何重大变动的详情。之后每三个月公布一次，直至恢复买卖或其上市地位被取消为止。公告还提醒，联交所可将已连续18个月暂停买卖的任何证券除牌。

title: 黄仁勋复职带动AI相关股票普涨 英伟达市值数小时增逾1万亿美元
summary: 英伟达宣布恢复黄仁勋总裁兼首席执行官职务并立即生效，AI相关股票应声普涨，英伟达股价一度上涨35%，创2000年以来最大盘中涨幅。受此带动，英伟达市值数小时内增逾1万亿美元。
source: 新浪财经 · 实时滚动
context: CEO复职这一罕见人事变动直接引爆AI板块行情，万亿美元级市值波动成为当日美股市场核心事件。
contentHtml:
英伟达恢复黄仁勋总裁兼首席执行官职务、并立即生效后，人工智能相关公司的股价大涨。

　　英伟达股价一度上涨35%，创2000年以来最大盘中涨幅，短短数小时内市值增加逾1万亿美元，并带动标普500指数和纳斯达克100指数走高。涨势还蔓延至芯片股，费城证券交易所半导体指数飙升13%；其他与人工智能基础设施交易相关的股票也上涨，包括能源供应商和工业企业。

　　Bokeh Capital Partners首席投资官Kim Forrest表示：“那件黑色夹克又回来了。大部分涨势都有其合理性，而且我们并没有对已经暴露出来的问题避而不谈。”

　　Miller Tabak + Co．首席市场策略师Matt Maley表示：“市场本来就已经处于超卖状态，之前的悲观情绪也非常高。”

　　不过，围绕人工智能交易更广泛的一些问题，并没有因为这次人事变动而得到解决。

　　他说：“不过，数据中心延期以及企业客户对定价的抵触并没有消失。因此，核心问题并没有改变。也正因为如此，从长期来看，这未必就是多头一直在等待的那个催化剂。”

　　Interactive Brokers首席策略师Steve Sosnick表示：“董事会似乎是在市场和政府的压力下让步了。这将安抚英伟达股东，甚至整个市场。但等新一届国会就位后，围绕黄仁勋、卢特尼克等人的一系列国会调查恐怕会接踵而至。”

contentHtml:
专题：英伟达官宣恢复黄仁勋总裁、CEO及董事会职务

　　核心要点

  • 美国总统特朗普表示，他已于周日晚间与复职的英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋通了话。
  • 特朗普在接受 记者埃蒙・贾弗尔斯电话采访时透露，在黄仁勋复职之前，他已经 “直接以及间接” 和英伟达董事会进行过沟通。
  • 特朗普称，董事会 “寻求国家安全风险层面的保证”，而他给出了这份保证。

　　美国总统特朗普周一早上表示，刚刚官复原职的英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋 “没有做错任何事”。

　　特朗普同时告诉埃蒙・贾弗尔斯：“我认为（英伟达）董事会做出恢复黄仁勋职务的决定，行事非常负责任。”

　　在电话采访中特朗普说道：“董事会的确向我方寻求关于国家安全风险的保证。”

　　“基于我们所掌握的全部信息 —— 而我们掌握的信息量很大，我们向他们作出了保证。”

　　特朗普表示，在英伟达董事会官宣黄仁勋复职之前的周日晚间，他就已经和黄仁勋通过话。

　　总统称：“我非常非常高兴，这家公司、董事会有勇气做出正确选择。过去两周，公司承受了巨大的损失。”

　　当被问及，上周黄仁勋辞职之后股市普遍大跌，这一因素是否推动他出面力促黄仁勋复职。特朗普回应：“或许有影响，但更重要的是长远考量。”

　　“关键在于，他脑子里还装着其他别人无从知晓的芯片设计方案。”

title: Z.ai 发布 7500 亿参数旗舰模型 GLM-5.4，跟随 OpenAI 布局循环 Transformer 架构
originalTitle: Z.ai follows OpenAI into loop transformer territory with its new 750B flagship model
author: Jonathan Kemper
summary: Z.ai 发布旗舰模型 GLM-5.4，将 7500 亿参数模型迁移至循环架构，让 28 层网络运行两次。公司称该设计能让其匹敌 2 至 3 万亿参数的模型，但目前基准成绩仅来自较小的 30B 测试模型。Z.ai 将 GLM-5.4 定位为"泛化编码"（Generalized Coding）的开端，代码还可生成视频、游戏和 CAD 模型。
context: 循环 Transformer 是 OpenAI 也在走的路线，Z.ai 以更少参数对标更大模型的策略值得行业关注。
contentHtml:
Z.ai is moving its flagship model to a loop architecture that runs some of its layers twice. With GLM-5.4, the company wants to mark the start of "Generalized Coding," where code also generates videos, games, and CAD models.

Following OpenAI, Z.ai is introducing GLM-5.4, its first large model built on a loop transformer. While standard language models use each layer once per pass, GLM-5.4 runs a block of shared layers multiple times, refining the intermediate results from the previous pass to make the network deeper without adding parameters. OpenAI has used a similar architecture since GPT-6 Astra. According to Z.ai, the 750-billion-parameter model reaches performance comparable to models with 2 to 3 trillion parameters.

The team retrained the GLM-5 base model released in February into a loop model that runs 28 layers twice. Loop models trained from scratch have so far performed worse than models without shared weights under the same compute budget, Z.ai writes.

Gates and shared caching keep the second pass manageable

Converting the model introduces a problem, Z.ai says. If the model simply overwrites intermediate states on each pass, activations grow sharply from round to round, leaving subsequent layers with values outside the range they were trained on.

To handle this, GLM-5.4 uses dedicated gates for each token and pass to control how much of the new output flows back into the data stream. According to Z.ai, the model builds context cautiously on the first pass and writes its changes back in full on the second. On difficult tokens, Z.ai says, the first pass steps in more strongly.

Because the second pass would otherwise double memory usage, both passes share the KV cache, the temporary memory for previously processed tokens. The second pass stores its own extra values only in a small local window. As a result, Z.ai says, the overhead compared to GLM-5.3 stays manageable even at a 1-million-token context.

To save on compute as well, the model uses sparse attention to pick the most relevant earlier tokens upfront rather than scanning the entire context every time, a standard technique. The second pass then reuses that selection from the first instead of making a new one. According to Z.ai, that yields nearly the same results as picking tokens separately on each pass. The company also says the model reaches up to 200 tokens per second off-peak and 70 to 80 tokens per second under load.

A looped 30B test model beats its baseline with shorter reasoning chains

Before rolling out the architecture in its flagship, Z.ai tested it on models with 1, 4, 30, and 750 billion parameters. For a direct comparison, the team used a 30B model built on the same architecture as the large base model. Both versions had the same parameter count, while the loop version received about 10 percent more training compute. Its biggest gain came on the AIME25 math benchmark, where scores jumped from 19.2 to 30.4 points. Scores on the expert-level science questions in GPQA-Diamond rose from 47.6 to 56.3 points, and on the AA-LCR long-context test they climbed from 40.3 to 47.7 points. Gains were smaller at just over three points on the MMLU-Pro knowledge test and on IFBench, which tests instruction following.

Responses also got shorter, shrinking 14.9 percent on MMLU-Pro, 11.7 percent on GPQA-Diamond, and just 2 percent on AIME25. Z.ai says part of the reasoning shifts out of the output tokens and into the loop's extra computational depth.

It is still impossible to judge how well GLM-5.4 actually performs, as Z.ai has published no benchmark scores for the 750B model and the figures in its blog post come solely from the 30B test. There are no independent evaluations from groups like Artificial Analysis either.

By Z.ai's own account, GLM-5.4's biggest weakness is overly long reasoning phases in which the model gets stuck, though the company says that extended double-checking improves accuracy.

Z.ai views GLM-5.4 as the starting point for "Generalized Coding," where the company says code becomes the foundation for tasks beyond traditional software development. To illustrate the idea, Z.ai shows a music video scored by the model itself, a six-axis robot arm it says GLM-5.4 designed in FreeCAD, a complete game, and an interactive 3D scene built from mathematical geometry and custom shaders.

1 / 4

Z.ai plans to release model weights and a much larger model

GLM-5.4 is available through the GLM Coding Plan, the ZCode coding environment, and Z.ai Chat, with an API set to follow and token pricing not yet announced. Z.ai plans to release the model weights after further safety testing, and it also announced a much larger model expected to arrive soon.

Shared layers date back to the Universal Transformer in 2018. In March, researchers in Bonn showed that looped transformers benefit from greater compute depth on math, while everyday knowledge benefits more from greater memory, the same trade-off Z.ai cites to explain its architecture. Thinking Machines also drew attention recently with Inkling 2 Mini because the loop model runs locally on Macs with at least 32 GB of RAM.

At 750 billion parameters, GLM-5.4 is nowhere near running on a laptop, but Z.ai is instead targeting the tier of Kimi K3.1 Pro and Qwen3.8-Max. At 2.8 trillion and 2.4 trillion parameters, respectively, those models are more than three times as large and require large amounts of compute.

For its predecessor GLM-5.3, Z.ai kept the existing base model and drew all of its gains from post-training. The company delayed releasing its weights because of the model's strong vulnerability-finding abilities, and Anthropic later found that GLM-5.3 could build exploits on its own, almost on par with Claude Mythos Preview.

title: 黄仁勋时隔12天重回英伟达CEO宝座 苹果乔布斯当年等了12年
originalTitle: 黄仁勋时隔12天重回英伟达CEO宝座 苹果乔布斯等了12年
summary: 英伟达董事会仅用12天就撤销罢免黄仁勋的决定，黄仁勋重回CEO职位。作为对照，苹果乔布斯当年重返CEO等了12年，而三年前的同一周，OpenAI撤换山姆·奥特曼后不到五天就完成了同样的复位。
source: 新浪财经 · 实时滚动
context: 董事会12天推翻罢免决定，与乔布斯12年、奥特曼5天的回归速度形成鲜明对比，凸显科技巨头治理波动对市场的冲击。
contentHtml:
作者：Jared Blikre

　　英伟达董事会只用了 12 天，就做出撤销罢免黄仁勋的决定。三年前的同一周，OpenAI 撤换山姆・奥特曼，完成同样的复位只用了不到五天。

　　几乎没人预料到黄仁勋复职的消息。周一早晨，就在英伟达发布官方复职公告的几分钟之前，预测市场 Polymarket 上，押注黄仁勋本月复职的概率仅约 3%。公告发布五分钟后，该概率飙升至 99%。

　　董事会全票通过决议，即刻恢复黄仁勋总裁、首席执行官以及董事职务，科莱特・克雷斯回归首席财务官岗位。董事会主席哈维・琼斯表示：“董事会认为，黄仁勋是领导英伟达的合适人选。” 英伟达股价暴涨超 30%。

　　黄仁勋的短暂下台代价惨重

　　从 11 月 11 日收盘（董事会接受黄仁勋辞职）至上周五，英伟达市值蒸发约 1.2 万亿美元，这期间还出现英伟达老款 GPU 价格逆势走高的现象。

　　硅谷之前就上演过相似戏码。2023 年 11 月一个周五下午，OpenAI 解雇奥特曼；周日微软向他抛出橄榄枝；OpenAI 约 770 名员工当中，超过 700 人威胁跟随他离职。到周二晚间，奥特曼重回 OpenAI。

　　奥特曼在 X 平台发文：“我热爱 OpenAI，过去几天我所做的一切，都是为了保全这个团队与我们的使命。”

　　虽然并非由本人发起，但民间也出现声援黄仁勋的浪潮。一份名为 “与黄仁勋站在一起” 的请愿书收集超 10 万签名，埃隆・马斯克也参与签名，其中有 5000 多份签名自称来自英伟达内部员工。请愿呼吁 “遵循正当程序，而非暴民式审判”。

　　当初促成奥特曼回归的关键力量是微软；而推动黄仁勋复职的是美国白宫。

　　董事会表示，美国政府高层给出意见，据此判定黄仁勋不存在国家安全风险，这成为他获得二次机会的关键。

　　但黄仁勋的回归和奥特曼有一处不同：奥特曼回来时，董事会已经完成大换血；黄仁勋面对的还是原班董事会，同时新增设立国家安全与出口控制委员会、启动首席合规官的招聘，还要接受针对 “遭境外情报机构盯上” 相关报道的独立调查。

　　乔布斯回归苹果耗费 12 年

　　史蒂夫・乔布斯 1985 年 9 月离开苹果，1997 年 9 月才回归担任临时 CEO。他回归首日，苹果股价上涨 2%；之后一年，苹果股价跑赢标普 500 指数，超额收益达到 65 个百分点。

　　大多数知名的创始人回归，开局都会获得华尔街一片叫好，但往后一年的表现却是好坏参半。英伟达本次盘前 30% 的涨幅，是下文统计图表里，其他几位 CEO 回归首日最大涨幅的三倍有余。

　　学术研究：“归位型 CEO” 的实际表现并不乐观

　　麻省理工斯隆管理学院的一项研究，统计 1992‑2017 年间标普 1500 成分股公司的 167 位重新上任的 CEO。研究发现，这类 CEO 任职期间，公司股价年均表现，要比首任 CEO 执掌时期低大约 10%；在技术迭代飞快的行业，差距会更大。 样本中，创始人 CEO 占全部 CEO 的 4%，但在 “归位复职 CEO” 群体里占比高达 44%。

　　黄仁勋接下来日程依旧紧张：12 月 1 日要参加众议院闭门问询，并且已经同意出席参议院银行委员会的公开听证会。

　　乔布斯后来把自己当年被赶出苹果的经历视作一份馈赠。

　　他在 2005 年斯坦福大学毕业演讲中说道：“我当时并未意识到，但事后证明，被苹果解雇，是发生在我身上最好的一件事。”

title: Sierra 完成 17.5 亿美元 F 轮融资，估值半年翻倍至 300 亿美元
originalTitle: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B within six months as demand for AI in CX takes off
author: Ivan Mehta
summary: 由前 Salesforce 联合 CEO Bret Taylor 联合创办的企业级客户体验公司 Sierra 周一宣布完成 17.5 亿美元 F 轮融资，估值在半年内翻倍至 300 亿美元。融资之际，市场对 AI 在客户体验领域应用的需求正快速升温。
context: 半年估值翻倍是 AI 应用层标志性融资事件，凸显企业级 AI 客服赛道的资本热度。
contentHtml:
Enterprise customer experience company Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles the company’s valuation to $30 billion. The new raise comes within six months of its previous round, which valued the company at $15 billion.

The new round was led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors who have led previous rounds, including Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV, and Tiger Global.

Enterprise automation is among the few areas where AI has seen rapid adoption. Sierra said that it currently serves almost 50% of Fortune 50 companies, and its clients include BNY, HSBC, Singtel, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase, Pearson, Next, and Cox Automotive. The company late last month said its outcome-based pricing model has helped it double its run-rate revenue to $400 million within five months.

That said, Sierra is working along similar lines as other customer experience players in the market, which is creating a platform to build agents and partner with model developers to provide choices to enterprises. As personal and work agents interact with enterprise systems, Sierra is also working on creating protocol definitions for agents with companies like Meta, Stripe, and Walmart.

Sierra will use the fresh cash build to its technology stack to layer agents for servicing, and hire more sales folks to sign and maintain enterprise contracts faster than its rivals.

Startups operating in the CX space have seen multi-million-dollar rounds come their way with soaring valuations. Voice AI company ElevenLabs is now valued at $22 billion; Decagon is valued at $4.5 billion; Wonderful is valued at $5 billion; and Parloa is valued at $3 billion. Multiple other startups have scored investments of more than $100 million.

During the HumanX conference in Amsterdam in September, Sierra co-founder Clay Bavor argued that despite the popular belief that AI-powered CX companies are replacing humans in contact centers, a majority of its customers are reassigning roles to existing employees.

title: 监管部门向券商下发两融新政通知：落实融资融券逆周期调节措施
originalTitle: 事关两融新政！监管部门向券商下发通知
summary: 11月23日，监管部门向券商下发《关于落实融资融券逆周期调节措施、提升风险管控有效性有关工作的通知》。该通知围绕落实两融逆周期调节措施、提升风险管控有效性提出要求，属两融领域新政。
source: 新浪财经 · 实时滚动
context: 两融直接关系市场杠杆资金与风险偏好，监管层此时下发通知对券商业务和资金面影响重大。
contentHtml:
来源：国际金融报

　　11月23日，记者获悉，监管部门向券商下发《关于落实融资融券逆周期调节措施、提升风险管控有效性有关工作的通知》（下称《通知》）。

　　为稳定资本市场、提振投资者信心，促进融资融券业务功能发挥，沪深京交易所于11月22日发布通知，明确融资保证金比例调整、客户交易行为规范等逆周期调节安排，相关措施自11月30日起正式实施。为确保相关工作平稳有序开展，引导投资者理性投资，切实有效防范风险，监管同步发布上述《通知》。

　　《通知》要求券商有效部署，确保政策稳妥实施。

　　一是做好保证金比例评估和调整。各公司要基于证券交易所公布的标准范围，结合公司内部相关风险管理政策，对保证金比例等实施动态管理与差异化控制。涉及修订或更新融资融券合同、签署补充协议的，应依规履行相关程序，并采取适当方式通知投资者，切实保障投资者合法权益。

　　二是及时完成系统调整。各证券公司要加强保障力度，及时完成系统参数调整，并根据证券交易所安排，完成系统测试验证，确保交易结算系统安全稳定。如确因无法克服的原因难以及时调整参数的，应做好应急预案，向投资者做好解释说明，不得因技术原因造成投资者投诉或纠纷。

　　三是做好政策解读和风险揭示。各证券公司要积极做好内部培训和投资者服务工作，确保分支机构和营业部员工、客户服务人员等正确理解政策内容，并向投资者做好解读。本次保证金比例调整同时适用于新开仓合约及存量合约，投资者不必了结存量合约即可适用新的指标，证券公司要将相关安排有效传达至投资者，避免因政策理解偏差引发不必要的调仓交易。此外，各证券公司要引导投资者秉持理性投资理念，根据自身风险承受能力，合理运用融资融券工具。

　　《通知》还强调要统筹风险，优化风险控制安排。各证券公司要持续保持对市场风险的警惕性和风险管理的审慎性，结合市场情况和公司实际，审慎确定风险容忍度和风险限额等风险管理指标，控制顺周期风险暴露，确保整体风险可测、可控、可承受。细化客户授信管理，加强对大额授信客户授信额度控制；优化标的和担保分类管理体系，持续完善担保证券可充抵保证金折算率动态调整机制，评估优化单一客户融资融券业务规模占比、单只担保股票市值占比、单一信用账户持仓集中度等风险控制指标，关注是否存在过度集中的结构性风险，提升业务管控有效性。

　　在市场波动期间，在与客户充分沟通、取得确认的情况下，可动态调整最低维持担保比例及追保平仓安排，以时间换空间，保持适度弹性。违约处置要稳妥审慎，注意处置金额、时点、节奏，避免早盘尾市等时点集中卖出，冲击市场和个股，自觉维护市场稳定。

　　《通知》也强调，压实责任，做好客户交易行为管理。各证券公司要认真落实证券交易所关于加强投资者融资融券交易行为管理的要求，对存在异常交易行为的投资者采取差异化的管控措施，从严适用保证金比例、可充抵保证金证券折算率等风险控制指标，审慎控制其授信规模及交易费率。对频繁发生异常交易行为的投资者，以及存在严重影响正常交易秩序的异常交易行为或者涉嫌违法违规交易行为的投资者，依法采取必要限制性措施。

　　黑崎资本首席战略官陈兴文对《国际金融报》记者分析，这份《通知》是配套约束券商执行环节的细化规则。一方面，保证金比例下调直接降低杠杆准入门槛，有望带动两融规模扩张，增厚券商利息收入；另一方面，配套规则明确动态管控、差异化授信、存量合约平稳衔接，保障政策红利顺畅传导。与此同时，对异常交易的管控力度同步加码，说明本次逆周期调节是带风控约束的杠杆优化，并非无底线放宽。

　　券商该如何在业务扩容与风控合规之间把握分寸？

　　“机会不在于两融余额的短期起落，而在于经营范式升级带来的估值重塑。”陈兴文进一步表示，第一，两融是券商资本中介业务的主战场，保证金比例下调意味着业务空间的直接扩容，头部券商凭借资金成本与渠道优势，最先受益。

　　第二，监管同步要求严控单一客户集中度、审慎把握追保平仓节奏、避免集中卖出冲击市场，抬高了粗放式经营的门槛，倒逼券商在业务扩张与风控合规之间寻求更高水平的平衡。

　　第三，风控能力、系统稳定性、研究服务实力构成的综合管理能力将成为券商的核心护城河，在新一轮行业分化中重新定价。

title: 英伟达尝试没有黄仁勋的日子，仅维持约两周
originalTitle: Nvidia tried life without Jensen Huang and it lasted about two weeks
author: Maximilian Schreiner
summary: 英伟达董事会已重新任命黄仁勋为总裁、CEO 兼董事会成员，立即生效。此前英伟达'没有黄仁勋'的日子只持续了约两周。
context: 英伟达是全球 AI 芯片龙头，黄仁勋的去留与回归是近期行业高度关注的重大治理事件。
contentHtml:
Nvidia's board of directors has reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board member, effective immediately. The decision was unanimous, Nvidia said in a press release, following talks with Huang and feedback from senior US government officials who concluded that his return poses no national security risk.

CFO Colette Kress had been running the company on an interim basis, and the stock had tanked during that period. President Donald J. Trump praised the decision on Truth Social, saying the US Attorney General found no evidence of wrongdoing by Huang. The move comes after reports that Huang had been targeted by foreign intelligence operations. An independent board committee is still investigating the matter with outside counsel.

The US government is also reviewing Nvidia's business dealings. Trump urged the company to keep looking into whether its export control compliance holds up. Nvidia has already set up a dedicated oversight committee for that purpose and is searching for a Chief Compliance Officer. Huang and the company said they'll continue cooperating with authorities and internal investigators. Nvidia's stock jumped more than 30 percent on the news.

title: Import AI 第482期：华为内核基准测试、空中无人机检测与国家实验室AI科学基准
